samples.question: For the ActionGenie incident involving UI freezing during bulk action suggestions, which customer ID was affected, what was the root cause, and what did the fix change?

evidence.text:
Thanks, @eid_92294e45! Lastly, we have a UI issue titled 'UI Freezes During Bulk Action Suggestions'. The interface becomes unresponsive when suggesting multiple actions in busy channels. This affects our User Interface & Frontend Performance, and it's impacting customer CUST-0088. @eid_92294e45, since you're already on the logging issue, can you also take this one?

Hi team, the bug titled 'UI Freezes During Bulk Action Suggestions' has been resolved. You can check the details in the PR here: https://github.com/salesforce/ActionGenie/pull/41.

https://github.com/salesforce/ActionGenie/pull/41

### Summary
The user interface was freezing when ActionGenie attempted to suggest multiple actions simultaneously in a busy Slack channel. This was due to the UI thread being blocked by synchronous processing of action suggestions.

### Changes Made
- Refactored the action suggestion logic to process asynchronously, ensuring the UI thread remains responsive.
- Implemented a callback mechanism to update the UI once suggestions are ready.
- Added error handling to manage any potential issues during asynchronous processing.

samples.ground_truth: CUST-0088. Synchronous processing blocked the UI thread. Process suggestions asynchronously and update the UI with a callback.

required_facts.cause: Synchronous processing blocked the UI thread.
required_facts.fix: Process suggestions asynchronously and update the UI with a callback.

- Implemented a more efficient task prioritization algorithm to ensure critical tasks are processed promptly.
- Enhanced the backend queue management to better handle high traffic scenarios.

### Summary
This pull request addresses the issue of duplicate log entries for manual actions, which was causing redundancy and confusion in the action history.

### Issue
The root cause of the problem was identified as a bug in the manual action logging function, which was triggered multiple times under certain conditions, such as network retries.

### Changes Made
- Updated the manual action logging function to ensure it logs actions only once, even in the event of network retries.
- Added a check to prevent duplicate entries by verifying the uniqueness of each log entry before logging.

samples.question: For the AnomalyForce incident involving gradual time-series drift generating false anomaly alerts, which customer ID was affected, what was the root cause, and what did the fix change?

evidence.text:
Great, thanks! Next, we have a 'Time Series Drift Misinterpretation'. The anomaly detection algorithm is misinterpreting gradual drifts as anomalies, leading to false positives for CUST-0025. @eid_63ea0ec4, can you take this one?

Hi team, the bug about incorrect anomaly detection due to time series drift misinterpretation has been resolved. You can check the details in the PR here: https://github.com/salesforce/AnomalyForce/pull/29.

https://github.com/salesforce/AnomalyForce/pull/29

### Summary of the Issue
The anomaly detection algorithm was incorrectly flagging gradual drifts in time series data as anomalies, resulting in false positive alerts. This was due to the algorithm's high sensitivity to slow-moving trends, which were not being adequately distinguished from sudden anomalies.

### Changes Made
- Implemented enhanced temporal smoothing techniques to better differentiate between gradual drifts and sudden anomalies.
- Adjusted the sensitivity parameters of the anomaly detection algorithm to reduce false positives.
- Updated the documentation to reflect the changes in the algorithm's behavior.

samples.ground_truth: CUST-0025. The detector was too sensitive to gradual trends and confused them with sudden anomalies. Improve temporal smoothing and adjust detector sensitivity.

required_facts.cause: The detector was too sensitive to gradual trends and confused them with sudden anomalies.
required_facts.fix: Improve temporal smoothing and adjust detector sensitivity.

samples.question: For the AnomalyForce incident involving inconsistent refresh rates across dashboard data sources, which customer ID was affected, what was the root cause, and what did the fix change?

evidence.text:
Awesome, thanks! Lastly, there's an issue with 'Inconsistent Data Refresh Rates in Multi-Source Dashboards'. This is causing outdated anomaly detection results for Customer CUST-0058. It's also in the User Interface & Data Visualization area. @eid_f0c7a505, looks like you're up again!

Hi team, the bug about inconsistent data refresh rates in multi-source dashboards has been resolved. You can check the details in the PR here: https://github.com/salesforce/AnomalyForce/pull/33.

https://github.com/salesforce/AnomalyForce/pull/33

### Summary
This pull request addresses the issue of inconsistent data refresh rates in multi-source dashboards within AnomalyForce. The problem was identified as asynchronous data fetching mechanisms that were not properly synchronized, leading to outdated anomaly detection results.

### Changes Made
- Implemented a synchronization mechanism for data fetching processes across different data streams.
- Introduced a centralized refresh controller to manage and harmonize the update intervals of all data sources.
- Refactored existing asynchronous calls to ensure they align with the new synchronization strategy.

samples.ground_truth: CUST-0058. Asynchronous data fetching was not synchronized across streams. Synchronize fetching and coordinate update intervals with a central refresh controller.

required_facts.cause: Asynchronous data fetching was not synchronized across streams.
required_facts.fix: Synchronize fetching and coordinate update intervals with a central refresh controller.
